response.content:
### Land and Property Records

Land and property records can place an ancestor in a specific location and reveal family relationships. Records include: deeds, abstracts, indexes, mortgages, leases, grants, sheriff sales, land patents, maps and more. For more information, see [Pennsylvania Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Land_and_Property "Pennsylvania Land and Property").

Land records in Allegheny County began in 1788. These records are filed with the [Department of Real Estate office](http://www.alleghenycounty.us/re/index.aspx) (formerly the Record of Deeds) in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. If your ancestor lived in the area which became Allegheny County, they may have filed land claims with Virginia when the area was know as the [District of West Augusta](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/West_Augusta_District,_Virginia "West Augusta District, Virginia").

*Online Land Indexes and Records*

* **1733 -1957** Pennsylvania State Archives, Records of the Land Office, [Warrant Registers, 1733-1957](http://www.phmc.state.pa.us/bah/dam/rg/di/r17-88warrantregisters/AlleghenySEPages/r17-88AllegSEPageInterface.htm), Allegheny County (South and East of the Ohio River)
* **1792 -1857** [Allegheny County Historical Deeds 1792–1857](https://pa_allegheny.uslandrecords.com/palr/) is a collection of documents recorded in deed books that described people who were involved in the slave trade in the early days of Allegheny County. This collection does *not* include all deeds recorded between 1792 and 1857.
* **1986 – present** Allegheny County offers [online access](https://pa_allegheny.uslandrecords.com/palr/) to indexes and images. Fees apply for copies.
* **1788 -1904** Deeds, 1788-1901; index, 1788-1904. [FS Library film 1532925 (first of 452 films)](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/531774) - images only; click on the camera icon to view images
* [Full-Text Search - Land Records](https://www.familysearch.org/search/full-text) at FamilySearch - index & images; dates, records, and places vary; [How to Search](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P00oMDsAsSw)

**Maps**

* Fishman, Joel. *The Warrantee Atlas of Allegheny County, Pennsylvania* Pittsburgh [Pennsylvania] Western Pennsylvania Genealogical Society, 1982. Originally published by the Pennsylvania State Land Office ca. 1914. [FS Library Large Folio 974.885 E7wa](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/138328) Digital version of the 1914 edition available at the University of Pittsburgh's ["Historic Pittsburgh Maps Collection."](https://historicpittsburgh.org/pittsburgh-maps)

### Local Histories

* *Allegheny County's Hundred Years.* 1888. By George H. Thurston. Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania : A.A. Anderson. **Online at:** [FamilySearch Digital Library](https://www.familysearch.org/library/books/records/item/505173-allegheny-county-s-hundred-years?offset=1), [Hathitrust](https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/008651472); [At various libraries (WorldCat)](https://search.worldcat.org/title/4173355).
* *History of Allegheny County, Pennsylvania : Including its Early Settlement.* 1889. By Thomas Cushing. Chicago, Illinois : A. Warner. **Online at:** [FamilySearch Digital Library](https://www.familysearch.org/library/books/records/item/615876-history-of-allegheny-county-pennsylvania-including-its-early-settlement-and-progress-to-the-present-time-a-description-of-its-historic-and-interesting-localities-its-cities-towns-and-villages-religious-educational-social-and-military-hi?offset=4), [Hathitrust](https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/009588802), [Internet Archive](https://archive.org/details/historyofalleghe01cush); [At various libraries (WorldCat)](https://search.worldcat.org/title/865644450).

### Migration

### Military Records

See more databases at *[Pennsylvania Military Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Military_Records "Pennsylvania Military Records")* and *[US Military Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/United_States_Military_Records "United States Military Records")*.

* **1885-1995** [Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, U.S., Veterans and Widows Burial and Death Records 1885-1995](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62942) at Ancestry — index & images ($)
* [Allegheny County Military Service](http://www.usgwarchives.net/pa/allegheny/pdf-files/PA,Alleg,Arch,Military,TOC.pdf) at [Allegheny County, Pennsylvania USGenWeb Archives](http://usgwarchives.net/pa/allegheny/) Includes 1835 Revolutionary War Pensioners, 1812 Pensioners, Biographies of original members of Civil War Co. D 149th PA.

***Revolutionary War***  
Men living in what is now Allegheny County (then Westmoreland and Washington counties) served in the [8th Pennsylvania Regiment](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/8th_Pennsylvania_Regiment_(Revolutionary_War) "8th Pennsylvania Regiment (Revolutionary War)").[[10]](#cite_note-10)

***Civil War***

* **1861-1865** [Pennsylvania, Register of Military Volunteers, 1861-1865](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3048335) at FamilySearch — [How to Use this Collection](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania,_Register_of_Military_Volunteers_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records "Pennsylvania, Register of Military Volunteers - FamilySearch Historical Records"); index
* **1865-1936** [Pennsylvania, Grand Army of the Republic Membership Records, 1865-1936](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2207723) at FamilySearch — [How to Use this Collection](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania,_Grand_Army_of_the_Republic_Membership_Records_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records "Pennsylvania, Grand Army of the Republic Membership Records - FamilySearch Historical Records"); index & images
* *Allegheny County, Pennsylvania in the War for the Suppression of the Rebellion, 1861-1865 : Roll of Honor, Defenders of the Flag, Attack on Fort Sumter, S.C., April 12, 1861, Surrender at Appomattox, Va., April 9, 1865* by Samuel M. Evans, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania: Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Hall, 1924] ***Online at:*** [FamilySearch Digital Books](http://www.familysearch.org/library/books/idurl/1/451131)
* *Black Civil War Soldiers, Allegheny County Pennsylvania* By Henry Hively; *Western Pennsylvania Genealogical Society Quarterly,* Vol. 17, No. 1. (Summer 1990):39. [FS Library Book 974.B2wg](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/1270067); [At various libraries (WorldCat)](https://search.worldcat.org/title/865947100)

**Regiments.** Men in Allegheny County served in various regiments. Men often joined a company (part of a large regiment) that originated in their county. Listed below are companies that were specifically formed in Allegheny County:  
- [70th Regiment, New York Infantry](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/70th_Regiment,_New_York_Infantry "70th Regiment, New York Infantry"), Company E

***World War II***

* **1933-1947** [Pennsylvania, Historical Society of Pennsylvania, World War II Casualty Cards, 1933-1947](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/4138682) at FamilySearch — [How to Use this Collection](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania,_Historical_Society_of_Pennsylvania,_World_War_II_Casualty_Cards_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records "Pennsylvania, Historical Society of Pennsylvania, World War II Casualty Cards - FamilySearch Historical Records"); index & images

### Naturalization and Citizenship

Naturalization records can contain information about immigration and nativity. Prior to 1906, it is rare to find the town of origin in naturalization records. For more information, see [Pennsylvania Naturalization](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Naturalization_and_Citizenship "Pennsylvania Naturalization and Citizenship")

Where to find Allegheny County naturalization records:

* **1734 -1906** Common Pleas Court #2
* **1799 -1894** Common Pleas Court #1
* **1799 -1906** Quarter Sessions Court
* **1906 - 1990** [Pennsylvania, Allegheny, Pittsburgh, Naturalization Card File Index, 1906-1990](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3037614) at FamilySearch — [How to Use this Collection](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania,_Allegheny,_Pittsburgh,_Naturalization_Card_File_Index_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records "Pennsylvania, Allegheny, Pittsburgh, Naturalization Card File Index - FamilySearch Historical Records"); index
* **1906 - Present** - Index only at Clerk's Office, Pittsburgh
* **Before 1906-Present** Federal Archives Records Center Archives Branch, Philadelphia[[11]](#cite_note-11)

*Online Naturalization Indexes and Records*

* **1795-1931** [Pennsylvania, Eastern District Petitions for Naturalization, 1795-1931](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1913395) at FamilySearch — [How to Use this Collection](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Eastern_District_Petitions_for_Naturalization_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records "Pennsylvania Eastern District Petitions for Naturalization - FamilySearch Historical Records"); index & images

* **1820-1906** [Index to Declarations and Petitions in the Western District of Pennsylvania, US Circuit and District Courts](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1192) located in *US Naturalization Records Indexes, 1794-1995* database on [Ancestry](http://search.ancestry.com) $, National Archives publication M1208

### Newspapers

Newspapers may contain obituaries, births, marriages, deaths, anniversaries, family gatherings, family travel, achievements, business notices, engagement information, and probate court proceedings.
Newspapers are often found in local or university libraries, historical or genealogical societies, or state archives in the area where the newspaper was published. See [Pennsylvania Newspapers](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Newspapers "Pennsylvania Newspapers") for more information.

### Obituaries

Obituaries are generally found in local newspapers where the person died or where family members lived. Local libraries or societies may have indexes or other sources.

### Other Records

***Poorhouse, Almshouse***  
[Allegheny County Workhouse Records, 1866-1971](http://www.phmc.state.pa.us/bah/dam/mg/mg197.htm). The site lists the records, including conduct books, 1870-1906, discharge and descriptive dockets, 1873-1971, escaped prisoners, 1882-1971, prison registers 1869-1951, and more. The records are at the [Pennsylvania State Archives](https://www.phmc.pa.gov/Archives/Pages/default.aspx).

### Periodicals

### Probate Records

Probate matters in Allegheny County are handled by the Orphans' Court and start when the county was created.

In addition to wills and administrations, the Orphans' Court also handles: audits of accounts of executors, administrators, trustees, and guardians; distribution of estates; appointments of guardians; adoptions; appeals from the Register of Wills; inheritance tax appeals, and various petitions and motions.

### Vital Records

Vital records are handled by the County Orphans' Court. Between the years 1852-1855 Pennsylvania made a failed attempt to record birth, marriage and death events at the county level. County marriage records were kept in earnest in 1885. Births and deaths, at the county level, were begun in 1893 and kept through 1905. For the most complete set of records, contact the County Orphans' Court.

#### Birth

Early births 1893–1905 are located at the County Orphans' Court. For more information, see [Pennsylvania Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Vital_Records "Pennsylvania Vital Records").

#### Marriage

#### Divorce

Divorce records are handled by the Department of Court Records Civil/Family Division (formerly the office of the Prothonotary). While no on-line indexes or records are available, records may be obtained on site or by correspondence. An index to [divorce records](https://dcr.alleghenycounty.us/indices/indices.html) is included in the Ejectment and Miscellaneous Index. Request at the main desk. Older records may be in storage and have to be ordered.

* [Allegheny County Divorce Index](http://files.usgwarchives.net/pa/allegheny/vitals/divorce-index.txt) from the USGenWeb Archives
* [Department of Court Records Civil/Family Division](https://dcr.alleghenycounty.us/indices/indices.html)
